surfaces.part: sign head cap (white lightbox top with teal underside)

answer.evidence: The width profile runs 6, 12, 14 (rows 2-8), 12, then 10 from row 10. The head therefore widens and narrows again, overhanging the 10-wide shaft by 2 px per side. The white rows 1-7 read as the top plate. Teal rows 8-9 below it act as the front edge and shadow, with a dark outline at row 10. The shaft (rows 10-25) is a tan front face carrying the number 4. The base (rows 26-30, width 12-16-12) is a flared plate with a lighter top band. The cap is somewhat boxy, with a chamfered rather than truly elliptical lower edge, but it does overhang and narrow at both ends.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style sign: a dark cap with a white round emblem, and a tan/ochre body carrying a '4' plate. At this size it reads clearly and sits with the references. Measured facts: 11 visible tones per tile (kiosk-a 12, bus-shelter-a 6, vending-a 20), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted rather than black. The outline is a dark brown/teal tone beside each material, not a uniform sticker line. The body ramp has about 4 steps (highlight, light, mid, shadow), a little shallower than the 5-6 steps in vending-a and kiosk-a, and the surface carries little grain beyond edge shading. It is simple and thin as a prop, but a careful artist would accept it next to kiosk-a and bus-shelter-a without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: sign head box (white face with teal shaded right side and bottom)

answer.evidence: The head (rows 0-9) is 14 px wide against a 10 px shaft, so it overhangs. The width profile 6, 12, 14 (rows 2-8), 12, 10 only chamfers the corners of a rectangle. The column scan shows the head as a white face (rows 2-7) over a teal shaded strip (rows 8-9), with a symbol drawn on the face. That is a face-on sign box, not a horizontal elliptical plate with back and front rim rows. There is no front-edge line with eave shadow that would mark a top plane. The shaft (rows 10-25) is a flat tan panel with a '4', outlined at rows 10 and 25, and the base (rows 26-30) is a front-facing collar. Nothing shows a top surface, so the object reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style exit sign with a cream/grey cap, an olive-tan body and a '4' numeral plate. It shows about 11 visible tones per full tile, which is on par with kiosk-a (12), above bus-shelter-a (6) and below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and reads as a dark version of the adjacent material, matching the references. The body has a light-to-dark side ramp of about 4 steps plus the cap highlight, which is a bit shallower than the 5-6 steps on the richer references. It is a small, simple, sparse object, so the lower density is not penalised heavily. A careful artist would accept it next to kiosk-a and bus-shelter-a, but it is thinner than vending-a. The tile-density and structure facts are at or above the accepted references, and the piece does not look sticker-like.
